ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has three layers of horizontal media, labeled in order as n1, n2, n3. A light ray enters medium 2 obliquely downward to the right from medium 1 above; at the first horizontal interface, the refracted ray in medium 2 is closer to the vertical normal. Then the ray enters medium 3 from medium 2; at the second horizontal interface, the refracted ray in medium 3 becomes closer to the horizontal line, that is, farther from the vertical normal. Reasoning: When light enters medium 2 from medium 1, it bends toward the normal, indicating that the refractive index of medium 2 is greater than that of medium 1, so the speed of light in medium 2 is smaller than that in medium 1, that is, v1 > v2. When light enters medium 3 from medium 2, it bends away from the normal, indicating that the refractive index of medium 3 is smaller than that of medium 2, so v3 > v2. Comparing medium 3 and medium 1, the light ray in medium 3 in the figure is farther from the vertical normal than the incident ray in medium 1, indicating that the refractive index of medium 3 is smaller than that of medium 1, so v3 > v1. Combining these, the speeds from large to small are v3 > v1 > v2.

raw_record.question_text: A beam of light passes from medium 1 to medium 2 to medium 3 as shown in the diagram. Order the speeds of light in media 1, 2, and 3 from greatest to least.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as three horizontal layers labeled n1, n2, and n3, with the light ray traveling downward/right. At the first boundary from medium 1 to medium 2, the ray bends closer to the vertical normal, so medium 2 has the larger refractive index and therefore the smaller light speed than medium 1. At the second boundary from medium 2 to medium 3, the ray bends away from the vertical normal and becomes nearly parallel to the boundary, so medium 3 has a smaller refractive index and therefore a larger speed than medium 2. To compare medium 3 with medium 1, observe that the ray in medium 3 is farther from the normal than the ray in medium 1, so medium 3 has lower refractive index and higher speed than medium 1. Therefore order speeds greatest to least as v3 > v1 > v2.

method.method_draft: First identify the boundaries in the image as parallel horizontal surfaces, so their normals are all vertical. Compare each ray segment’s angle with this same vertical normal: in medium 2 the ray is steepest/closest to vertical, in medium 1 it has an intermediate angle, and in medium 3 it is closest to horizontal/farthest from vertical. For a ray crossing parallel layers, Snell’s law gives n sin(theta) as the same constant across the layers, where theta is measured from the normal. Thus the segment with the largest theta has the smallest n and largest speed, while the segment with the smallest theta has the largest n and smallest speed. Since theta3 > theta1 > theta2, the refractive indices satisfy n3 < n1 < n2, so the speeds satisfy v3 > v1 > v2.
